articles.title: John Aloisi’s Chengdu choke to blow title chances on final day of Chinese season
articles.summary: Chengdu lose their final four games to give up a 12-point lead. Dalian Yingbo FC claim title on drama-laden day in China. John Aloisi’s Chengdu Rongcheng let the Chinese Super League title slip from their grasp on the last day of the season, losing their fourth consecutive game as rivals Dalian…
body: Dalian completed a remarkable comeback by overhauling Chengdu’s lead, which once stood at 12 points, with Aloisi’s side picking up just one point in their last five matches. On the league’s final day, Chengdu lost 3-2 to Shandong Taishan, while Dalian’s 3-1 victory over Tianjin Tiger earned Li ⁠Guozu’s side ​the trophy.

The results saw the two teams finish level on 52 points, ​with Dalian winning the title on ‌a better head-to-head record ‌after recording a pair of wins over Chengdu, including in the penultimate ‌round of matches.

Dalian still needed to win on Sunday while hoping Chengdu lost, and Aloisi’s side went two goals down in Jinan when Raphael Merkies and Guilherme Madruga struck in the 15th and 23rd minutes respectively.

Felipe Silva pulled one back for Chengdu with seven minutes remaining ‌in the first half and, while Cryzan restored Shandong’s two-goal advantage in the 63rd minute, Wellington Silva’s 79th minute strike ​set up a tense finish.

articles.title: Abbi Church powers Australia to win over spirited Fiji as hosts reach Women’s Rugby League World Cup final
articles.summary: Church scores four tries as Australia beat Fiji Bulikula 30-14. Jillaroos will face New Zealand in the final next weekend. The Jillaroos survived an almighty scare from Fiji in the World Cup semi-final, securing a place in the tournament decider against New Zealand at Lang Park next week despite a…
body: Driven by the exquisite, unpredictable playmaker Luisa Yaranamua – 23 and yet to play an NRLW match – and supported by powerful, committed teammates, Fiji led for much of the first half and were level with the Jillaroos at half-time.

It took a quadruple from Australian winger Abbi Church – including a spectacular put-down from a Tarryn Aiken kick and a late runaway – in a more composed second half performance from the Jillaroos to settle the contest. Yet they go into next week’s final with an injury concern over their other winger Jaime Chapman, who was taken off with a quad injury after scoring.

While the defeat will hurt the inspired Fijians, who had tears running down their faces during their anthem and delivered a passionate pre-match hymn, their first women’s World Cup will not be forgotten. Their valiant effort against Australia, and another narrow loss to the Kiwi Ferns earlier in the tournament, have proved international women’s rugby league is alive despite the dominance of the Jillaroos.

articles.title: Julián Alvarez’s Atlético redemption arc in full focus for visit of Barcelona
articles.summary: Top spot is up for grabs in Sunday’s heavyweight clash as the Spider faces the team that tried to trap him last summer. Julián Alvarez said sorry but forgiveness must be earned on the field and Sunday would be the perfect place. At 9pm at the Metropolitano, Atlético Madrid play Barcelona.
body: He has beaten them before. Last season, Atlético knocked Barcelona out of the Copa del Rey and Champions League. Alvarez scored both times but beneath the surface something had shifted in him and by the time the World Cup came round he admitted his desire to leave for Catalonia. That day, after Argentina beat Algeria, he didn’t name Barcelona and he didn’t need to; everyone knew. “It’s not the time to talk about this but nor can I hide,” he said. “I spoke with the people I needed to and the best thing for everyone is a transfer.”

They were still whistling too. Stuck, Alvarez had some making up to do, if only out of convenience, if only for a little while. He left Fernando Hidalgo, the agent whose exit strategy had failed, whom Atlético’s chief executive accused of having led Alvarez astray and who responded by calling the club “liars”. That helped, handing over someone to blame. He also played a bit more and a bit better, if not much to begin with. He at last scored a goal against Stuttgart on 20 October and four days later did it again, this time at home in a 1-0 win over Deportivo A Coruña. “I would like to apologise to our people for my words at the World Cup,” he said after.

articles.title: Is there something missing despite Rangers' impressive form?
articles.summary: Rangers made it 12 games without defeat in all competitions with a 2-0 win at St Mirren on Saturday, but Ibrox legend Kris Boyd believes there is "something missing".
body: Rangers are unbeaten in their past 12 matches in all competitions, winning 10 of them, and moved to within a point of the Scottish Premiership summit after Saturday's 2-0 win away to St Mirren.
They thoroughly deserved their victory. They have the best defensive record in the top flight and the third best attacking record, but it feels as though they are not playing to their full potential.
In Paisley, Derek McInnes' side never quite put the game to bed despite a host of chances and St Mirren should really have pulled one back in the closing stages.
"There's still not that element of control," former Celtic striker Chris Sutton said on Sky Sports.

articles.title: I haven't thrown anyone under the bus - Khawaja
articles.summary: Usman Khawaja says he has "not thrown anyone under the bus" with revelations about the sandpaper scandal that engulfed the Australia team in 2018.
body: In his autobiography - Sabr - and in an interview with the Sydney Morning Herald, Khawaja claimed the entire team should take responsibility for the plot to use sandpaper on the ball in the third Test against South Africa eight years ago.
At the time, the only players punished were captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and opener Cameron Bancroft.

Speaking in videos posted on Instagram on Sunday to clarify his comments, Khawaja said: "You would have seen when I mentioned it was all of us, that's implying that whether we like it or not, we are all responsible for what happened together.

"But now that everyone's talking, am I going to deny that everyone knew? Nah, I won't deny that, either. But I never speak on behalf of anyone else in my book, contrary to what the headlines in clickbait media would have you think."

articles.title: English hopes fade as Pelaez hits hole-in-one en route to title in China
articles.summary: England's Mimi Rhodes, Charlotte Heath and Annabell Fuller saw their hopes fade on the last day of the Aramco China Championship as Spain's Ana Pelaez stormed to her second Ladies European Tour title with a nine-under round that included a hole-in-one.
body: Heath shared the lead with Pelaez's compatriot Luna Sobron on 16 under after round three in Shenzhen, with Rhodes one shot back and Fuller three strokes adrift.

Fuller stared superbly on Sunday with four birdies in her first six holes lifting her to 16 under but she then registered three bogeys on her back nine ahead of a closing birdie to end up on 14 under and in ninth spot after a one-under day, six shots behind Pelaez.

With Heath only able to card an even-par 73, mixing two birdies with as many bogeys, Rhodes, a three-time winner on the Ladies European Tour in 2025, was the highest-placed of the English contingent, finishing in outright second on 17 under.
The 24-year-old, who made her Solheim Cup debut in September as Team Europe defeated Team USA in the Netherlands, registered birdies at four and 17 as she signed for a blemish-free, two-under 71.

articles.title: Australia set up fifth straight final vs New Zealand after overcoming Fiji
articles.summary: Defending champions Australia set up a fifth consecutive Women's Rugby League World Cup final against New Zealand after coming from behind to beat a spirited Fiji in Sydney.
body: The Jillaroos, who have beaten New Zealand in the last three finals since they were thumped 34-0 by the the Kiwi Ferns in the 2008 showpiece in Brisbane, won 30-14 against Fiji as Abbi Church notched four tries.

Fiji opened up a shock 8-0 lead as Luisa Yaranamua followed a penalty by scoring a try that she also converted, leaving the home side trailing for the first time in the tournament, but Australia made it 8-8 by the break and then dominated the second half.
Australia had won all three of their group games, scoring 242 points and conceding just six, but this was a real test.
Church leapt over the line for the hosts' first try after 25 minutes before Tamika Upton doubled that tally four minutes later to level the scores.

body: Batter Khawaja, who retired from international cricket earlier this year, said he had made a "promise" to David Warner - one of three players banned in the wake of 'Sandpapergate', along with Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft - that he would "tell the truth".
In the Cape Town Test against the Proteas eight years ago, Bancroft was caught on camera trying to rough up one side of the ball with sandpaper to try and make it swing through the air.

The bowling attack for the Cape Town Test - Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Nathan Lyon and Josh Hazlewood - released a statement in 2021 denying any knowledge of the plot, while Cricket Australia has always asserted only Smith, Warner and Bancroft knew about it.
Khawaja said in a video on Instagram: "I haven't ⁠thrown anyone under the bus.

articles.title: White: Billam-Smith was stopped too soon
articles.summary: Chris Billam-Smith finished the fight on his feet, shaking his head in protest, when referee Lee Every halted him in the seventh round against Cheavon Clarke.
body: No one before had seen Billam-Smith in that kind of predicament. He'd never previously been dropped let alone stopped.
But Cheavon had put him down twice in that round before finishing matters against an old amateur rival.
Billam-Smith wanted to carry on and Zuffa Boxing promoter Dana White agreed, saying: "I thought it was early."
Clarke backed the referee's call, convinced he had the former WBO world champion in severe distress.

articles.title: Bayern boss confirms interest in Mohya
articles.summary: Bayern Munich board member for sport Max Eberl has confirmed that the German champions are monitoring Borussia Mönchengladbach prodigy Wael Mohya. However, he played down reports that Bayern have already made an initial approach to the youngster’s representatives.
body: “In general, FC Bayern keeps an eye on every young German talent. We are monitoring the boy,” Eberl told Sky on Saturday.
“However, we have not yet spoken with the player, his agency or Borussia Mönchengladbach.”
Bayern are among several clubs keeping tabs on Mohya, who received his first senior Germany call-up earlier this week.

articles.summary: Vanja Milinković-Savić replaces Alex Meret in goal for Napoli against leaders Lazio, with Noa Lang behind Rasmus Højlund, while Nuno Tavares shakes off a muscular problem to start for Gennaro Gattuso’s side. Napoli vs.
body: Napoli vs. Lazio kicks off at 12:30 CET [11:30 GMT] on Sunday at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, with Luca Pairetto as referee.

Gennaro Gattuso returns to Naples as leader of Serie A. His Lazio side are still unbeaten after 10 games, with nine wins and a draw, and are top on 28 points. Roma’s 3-0 win over Sassuolo on Saturday cut their lead to a single point, so a win today would put the Biancocelesti back four points clear before the international break.

It’s a very different picture for Napoli. Max Allegri’s side are 14 points behind today’s opponents on 14 and come into the game after losing 2-0 at Juventus and 4-1 at Porto in the Champions League, which has put the coach under growing pressure.

Napoli have a long injury list. Giovanni Di Lorenzo, Leonardo Spinazzola, Stanislav Lobotka, Benoit Badiashile, David Neres, Alisson Santos, Costantino Favasuli and Alessandro Buongiorno are all out, and Mathias Olivera is not fully fit but still starts.
